nome: Burning and Suppression of Solids - II
sintesi: Study ignition, flame growth, flame spread, and extinction limits for solid fuels burning in low-velocity forced flows in microgravity.
risultato_chiave: BASS-II results contribute to the combustion computational models used in the design of fire detection and suppression systems.
fonte_note: PSI-25 page (DOI, platform, airflow up to 40 cm/s, test table) | NTRS 20150019858 and NTRS 20210011385 (BASS-II Summary Report): "O2 concentrations in the MSG working volume were varied during the testing from ambient ISS O2 levels (~21 percent O2) down to ~14 percent O2 for very near limit flames." | Test table on the PSI page: calibrated initial O2 22.2% in the rows shown.
note: Oxygen 14-22.2%: 14-21% from NTRS, upper bound 22.2% from the test table on the PSI page. Minimum flow empty: the source gives only the maximum. Flow: the PSI page says up to 40 cm/s; the NTRS summary report says ~55 cm/s without restrictors and ~35 cm/s with two restrictors: we kept the PSI page value. Pressure not stated as a test condition: empty.

sintesi: Determine how rapidly a large scale fire grows in low-gravity and investigate the low-g flammability limits.
risultato_chiave: Saffire-1 experiments were performed on the Cygnus resupply vehicle after it deberthed from the ISS.
fonte_note: PSI-98 page: Saffire-I run at an air flow of 20 cm/s; test table: O2 21.5-21.7 (S1) and ~21.5 (S2) | NTRS 20170000230: "The oxygen concentration in the Cygnus vehicle will be nearly 21% by volume"; NTRS 20170001636: "Saffire-I will be conducted at an air flow velocity of 20 cm/s" (pre-flight papers).
note: Platform: the Flight Platform field of the page says ISS, but the page text says the experiment ran on the Cygnus resupply vehicle after it left the ISS; we use Cygnus. Pressure not stated: empty. NTRS 20220002714 (Saffire-IV) and 20240007488 (Saffire-VI) are other missions: not used.

sintesi: Study droplet combustion and extinction characteristics in microgravity to improve fire safety and combustion efficiency.
fonte_note: PSI-69 page (DOI, platform, test table) | NTRS 20130014061: "The ambient oxygen concentration varied from a high value of 30% by volume to as low as 12%"; "at primarily two different ambient pressures (0.7 and 1 atm)". | NTRS 20150023456 (FLEX Detailed Results): "Most of the tests were conducted at pressures between 0.7 and 1 atm"; "various pressures between 0.70 and 3.05 atm".
note: O2 12-30% and 0.7-1 atm (10.3-14.7 psia) are the conditions of most tests (NTRS 20130014061 and 20150023456 agree). The full FLEX test range is 0.70-3.05 atm (up to 44.8 psia), above the 30 psia schema limit: not reported. Flow: quiescent ambient, empty.

sintesi: Evaluate material flammability limits in microgravity using a broader suite of solid materials.
risultato_chiave: Saffire-II tested multiple materials to establish flammability screening protocols.
fonte_note: PSI-99 page: Cygnus platform; table: air flow 20 cm/s, O2 ~21.5-22.1% | NTRS 20200000557 (article DOI 10.1016/j.combustflame.2018.10.016): "Microgravity experiments were conducted during NASA's Spacecraft Fire Experiment (Saffire II), on board the Cygnus spacecraft at 100 kPa with an air flow velocity of 200 mm/s."
note: 100 kPa = 14.5 psia; 200 mm/s = 20 cm/s. The DOI column holds the PSI dataset DOI; the NTRS paper has its own article DOI (10.1016/j.combustflame.2018.10.016). Sensors left empty: not verified.

nome: Structure and Liftoff in Combustion Experiments
sintesi: Examine flame stabilization, liftoff, and blowout limits in laminar jet flames in microgravity.
fonte_note: PSI-106 page (DOI, platform) | NTRS 20150011070: "five coflow velocities (peak coflow velocity vO,max approximately equals to 18, 39, 48, 54, and 71 cm/s) under both microgravity and normal gravity"; NTRS 20140017780: "nominal air coflow of 18 cm/s".
note: SLICE is not one of the allowed project values: set to 'altro' (other). Flow = peak air coflow velocity (18-71 cm/s). The papers deal with methane flames (CH4 70-100%); the fuel field (propane) comes from the PSI page: to be checked. Oxygen and pressure not stated: empty.
